Find your way around the tracker, understand the numbers, and turn your tour history into a learning plan. This guide is the same for everyone.

Getting started Find a feature Reading the numbers Definitions Common questions

Getting started

  1. Choose a player. Search for a player on the home page. Use Change User in the top bar to open someone else’s dashboard.
  2. Choose your context. W / U selects Watched or Usual tour records. Using data changes the history window on supported pages. EN / JP changes anime titles where available.
  3. Choose your goal. Start with Latest Tour to review a game, Knowledge to explore strengths, or Relearn Tracker to find songs to practise.

The ant icon includes ANT stats on supported views. Full opacity means on; faded means off. A locked control means that view uses a fixed context.

Where to find things

Overview

General gives a recent snapshot and historical highlights. Latest Tour compares the latest tour with your previous 3 or 10 tours and shows Solos, Doubles, and Franchise Repeats. Stats Summary compares broader strengths; Weekly Performance shows weekly results and changes.

Performance

Explore guess-rate trends, Lives Taken / Saved, Onlist/Offlist, Rigs Missed, and Composite charts. Use this section to see how your performance changes over time.

Knowledge

Use Artist, Franchise, and Tag Familiarity to explore what you know and inspect song attempts. Franchise Familiarity groups related anime entries. Seasonal Comparison compares release seasons.

Recommendations

Relearn Tracker finds songs you previously got correct but missed most recently. By Wrong Guess ranks songs by misses; By never correct focuses on songs you have not answered correctly in the available history. Playlists appear for players with access.

Social

Synergy compares correct-answer overlap with another player. Rivals and Team Contributions explore player comparisons and team results. Rig / List analysis explores the songs associated with your list.

Other tools

Search songs to inspect individual histories, or Search song frequency to explore how often songs appear. Player database compares players with combined year and genre/tag filters. Single Tour opens a particular tour’s results.

Reading the numbers

Attempts and song familiarity answer different questions

A tour’s guess rate describes your correct answers in that tour. Repeated appearances can count as separate attempts. The same song appearing five times is five attempts.

Genre summaries, Tag Familiarity, Franchise Familiarity, and Player database comparisons use the last-two-attempt approach: a song entry counts once and is treated as correct if either of its last two tracked attempts was correct. A single tracked attempt uses that result.

Example: wrong → correct → wrong is three attempts with one correct answer, but the song counts as correct under the last-two rule.

Tour % is a song reference

Tour % comes from the song’s stored Watched or Usual tour-correct percentage. It is a shared reference for the song, accounting for overplayed songs, rather than your personal correct / attempts percentage.

Difficulty is a separate catalog value. It is not your personal guess rate and is not another name for Tour %.

Compare like with like: check the mode, history window, denominator, and any minimum sample requirement before comparing two numbers.

Standardized scores depend on the baseline

A z-score is (value − mean) / standard deviation. Zero is the baseline average; +1 is one standard deviation above it and −1 is one below.

Latest Tour: the latest value is compared with the previous 3 or 10 comparable tours, excluding the latest tour. Combined trend: each metric is standardized against its own history. Stats Summary: standardized metrics compare recent performance against other players.

These charts use different reference groups, so their z-scores need not match. If a metric cannot be compared, Latest Tour explains why above the chart.

Dates and scoring systems matter

Watched and Usual are separate datasets. Some metrics are unavailable in one mode or time period. Usefulness and rank use different scoring systems before 2026.

The Combined overview trend only includes usefulness and rank from 2026 onward, and does not show ANT usefulness or rank. Its view selection is unavailable with ANT selected.

Some cards explicitly use a recent 10-tour window even when another history range is selected. Hover the info icon beside a title for that card’s calculation.

Definitions at a glance

OP / ED / IN
Opening, ending, and insert song. A number such as OP2 identifies the song’s opening/ending sequence.
Pattern squares
Green means correct; red means wrong. Each square represents a tracked attempt. Hover a square for its date where available. Some views limit how many attempts are displayed.
Onlist / rig
A song associated with the player’s list in the recorded data. Offlist refers to songs outside that list. Historical list associations can differ from a player’s current anime list.
Solo / double
A song answered correctly by one or two players. Latest Tour’s Solos and Doubles show your correct answers from eight-player song results; “You & player” names the other correct player on a double.
Franchise repeat
Two or more song appearances from the same anime or related franchise in the songs you encountered during the latest tour. Other matches in the tour that you did not play are excluded.
Correct > 1 / Wrong / All
In Franchise Repeats, Correct > 1 requires at least two correct answers; Wrong requires every answer to be wrong; All includes every repeated franchise. The selected franchise’s results include all its encountered songs.
W-T-L
Wins, ties, and losses, in that order. This describes team match results, rather than individual song accuracy.
Elo / rank
The tour’s recorded player rating is shown beside player names. It is a separate measure from guess rate; do not read it as a percentage of songs answered correctly.
Lives taken / saved
Team-impact measures reported in the tour results. The site’s Net Lives Contribution card averages lives saved + lives taken over the last 10 games.
Usefulness
A tour-reported performance measure, distinct from guess rate. Its scoring system changed before/after 2026, so direct comparisons across those periods need care.
Momentum / consistency
Momentum compares the last 3 guess rates with the last 10. The Overview consistency card measures recent variation; lower means steadier. Artist radar metrics have their own definitions.
Sample point
A playback start point attached to a recorded song appearance. Play sample uses the available sample; Play song plays the recording normally.

Common questions

How do I inspect a chart?

Hover a point or bar for details. On charts with a legend, click a legend item to show or hide that series. Data and trend lines may have separate legend entries. Where zoom is supported, drag over a range and use the reset control to return.

How do I practise or export relearn songs?

Open Recommendations → Relearn Tracker. Use All / Onlist / Offlist to filter songs and Play / Links to change the controls. The download icon opens Watched / Usual / All, list filters, and the maximum number of latest songs. Download ZIP saves audio; Export for CSL uses the AMQ+ import format. The selected latest songs follow the tracker’s order.

How do I navigate Franchise Repeats?

Select a cover or use the left/right controls. When the selector has keyboard focus, use ← / → to move between franchises. The row below shows songs from the selected franchise. Choose All to see every repeated franchise.

Why is a view empty or locked?

The selected player, mode, or time window may have no qualifying data. Some pages require a minimum sample count. Rig / List analysis in All tours requires at least 300 qualifying rig-song samples; try another Using data mode when that minimum is not met. A dash or unavailable message should not be read as zero.

Does Synergy measure list overlap?

The Only you / Both correct / Only them bars compare correct-answer overlap, not anime-list overlap. All seen songs and Shared seen songs use different sets of encountered songs, so read the info icon for each bar.

Standardized Metrics Compares your average from up to your last 10 eligible tours against player averages in the selected Watched or Usual mode. 0 is average, +1 is one standard deviation better, and -1 is one standard deviation below average. Avg / 8 is flipped so lower values score higher. Usual has no scores for Onlist, Offlist, or Offlist ERigs. Unavailable metrics keep their category names but have no bar.

Genre Genre percentages count each song only once instead of counting repeated attempts. For each song, if either of the last two attempts is correct, that song is treated as correct.
Hover a genre to see details.

    Player comparison

    Shows overlap between you and the target player. Overlap is measured by what you both got correct(thus it is NOT rig overlap). The left displays unique songs you got correct, while the right displays unique songs the target player got correct.
    Their rig, you hit Songs from their rig that you answered correctly. For "Unique rig", shows only songs that you got unique to their list. For "Include shared rig", it can include songs from your list that are in the selected player's list. Both players don't have to be in the same game.
    Your rig, they hit Songs from your rig that they answered correctly. For "Unique rig", shows only songs that they got unique to your list. For "Include shared rig", it can include songs from their list that are in your list. Both players don't have to be in the same game.
